item.title: UK Construction Downturn Eases as Demand Resurfaces, PMI Shows
item.description: British construction firms showed signs of stabilizing from a plunge in activity over the spring with housebuilding falling at the slowest pace in nine months.S&P Global's construction purchasing managers' index climbed to a four-month high of 44.7, up sharply from post-pandemic lows of below 40 in the previous three months. item.description: What's next on the currency market to-do list?

item.title: Odd Lots: Brad Setser on the US’s Yen Intervention (Podcast)
item.description: Last week, the US joined forces with Japan to try to stop the yen’s slide. It’s the first time the two sides have intervened in the Japanese currency in 15 years, and in many ways it was an unprecedented and unusual move, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent choosing to sell euros (as opposed to dollars) and the use of a little-known Federal Reserve repo facility. item.title: SoftBank Books $8.5 Billion Gain on Intel to Beat Estimates
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. reported a smaller-than-expected decline in quarterly net income, lifted by a big boost from its stake in Intel Corp. while it awaits an OpenAI listing.

item.title: Nintendo Tops Estimates With Tariff Refunds and Switch 2 Games
item.description: Nintendo Co. reported stronger-than-expected earnings buoyed by tariff refunds from the US and strong sales of a pair of in-house titles for its flagship Switch 2 console.

item.title: German June Factory Orders Jump More Than Economists Predict
item.description: German factory orders rose by more than analysts forecast, another sign that a long-awaited recovery in Europe’s biggest economy may finally be taking hold.

item.title: East African Breweries Profit Grows Fastest in Four Years
item.description: East African Breweries Plc’s annual profit grew at the fastest pace in four years, even as accelerating inflation in its home market Kenya eroded spending power.

item.title: OpenAI Asks Judge to Toss Apple’s Trade Secrets Lawsuit
item.description: OpenAI is asking a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed by Apple Inc. accusing the artificial intelligence company of stealing trade secrets, saying that the iPhone maker’s allegations are meritless.

item.title: WPP Profit Beats Analysts’ Estimates on Cost-Cutting Efforts
item.description: WPP Plc reported first-half profits that beat analysts’ estimates, driven by the advertising agency’s cost-cutting efforts in a sluggish market.

item.title: Swiss Re Profit Beats Estimates as Re-Insurer Boosts Cost Cuts
item.description: Swiss Re AG’s first-half profit beat estimates as the re-insurer saw all key business units perform in line with targets, while the firm announced a fresh round of cost cuts.

item.title: Zurich Insurance Earnings Boosted by Global Data Center Demand
item.description: Zurich Insurance Group AG reported a 13% gain in profit for the first half of 2026 as it saw accelerating demand across all businesses, boosted by global data center and energy infrastructure demand.

item.title: Commerzbank Unveils €1.2 Billion Buyback as UniCredit Talks Loom
item.description: Commerzbank AG unveiled a fresh share buyback as Chief Executive Officer Bettina Orlopp seeks to demonstrate that her strategy delivers strong returns while Italian rival UniCredit SpA is preparing to control.

item.title: Siemens Raises Earnings Outlook on Software, Data Center Gains
item.description: Siemens AG raised its earnings expectations for a second time this year on a surge in data center spending and higher returns from selling software to industry.

item.title: Deutsche Telekom Raises Share Buyback By Up to €3 Billion
item.description: Deutsche Telekom AG, Europe’s biggest phone carrier, raised its share buyback program by as much as €3 billion ($3.5 billion) in 2026 after reporting second-quarter results in line with expectations.

item.title: Social Media Ban: How Do Limits For Children and Teens Work?
item.description: Since Australia barred under-16s from using social media in late 2025, more than two dozen countries have either enacted their own bans or are weighing similar restrictions.

item.title: Nickel Drops After Report Indonesia to Lift Quota for Major Mine
item.description: Nickel fell to the lowest level since mid-July on renewed speculation that Indonesia will grant a higher ore-production quota to one of the country’s largest mines, potentially boosting supplies.

item.title: Russia’s War Economy Is Fueling Pay Gains Companies Can’t Afford
item.description: As President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine extends for a fifth year, Russian businesses can no longer afford to keep pace with the Kremlin’s war machine in the wage race.

item.title: Czechs Set to Hold Rates as Price Pressures Signal Cautious Tone
item.description: Czech policymakers will likely leave interest rates unchanged, keeping the door open to further monetary tightening as persistent domestic inflation risks outweigh a recent drop in oil prices.

item.title: Japan 30-Year Bond Sale Brings Relief Amid Fiscal Concerns
item.description: A sale of 30-year Japanese bonds drew firm demand on Thursday, delivering some calm to a market that’s been buffeted by currency turmoil and worry over the government’s debt load.

item.title: KRW/USD: Korean Won Rises to Highest Since October on Exporters Dollar Sales
item.description: The South Korean won rose to the strongest level in almost 10 months as exporters converted their dollar earnings into the local currency.

item.title: Retailer Dien May Xanh Rises in Trading Debut as Market Rebounds
item.description: Dien May Xanh Investment JSC, an electronics retail chain unit of Mobile World Investment Corp., rose in its trading debut on Thursday amid a broader market rebound.

item.title: Takaichi Says Return to 8% Food Sales Tax Key for Market Trust
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi flagged the importance of restoring the 8% sales tax rate on food after two years to maintain trust among market participants.

item.title: Korea in Race to Keep Chips Edge as China Presses, Minister Says
item.description: South Korea risks losing its edge in semiconductors unless it helps chipmakers accelerate investment, as China pours unprecedented resources into the industry and intensifies the global technology race, Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said.

item.title: China Steel Group Says Push for Yuan-Pricing Would Help Iron Ore
item.description: China’s main steel-industry group called for greater use of yuan-denominated index pricing in the iron ore market, saying such a shift would better reflect supply and demand in the top user of the commodity.

item.title: DeepSeek Plans ‘Significant’ Price Increase for AI Services
item.description: DeepSeek plans to implement a significant price increase across its AI services, an unusual shift from the disruptive Chinese player that has put pressure on US and domestic rivals.

item.title: Traders in India Dial Back October Rate-Hike Bets After Dovish RBI Speak
item.description: The earliest that the market is now anticipating a rate hike is December.

item.title: SK Hynix Hit by Another 30% Pre-Market Flash Crash on Nextrade
item.description: Chip giant SK Hynix Inc. suffered its second short-lived share plunge in about a week, raising fresh questions about trading volatility on South Korea’s alternative stock exchange.

item.title: Fed’s Daly Supported Rate Decision, Warns of Inflation Risks
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said she supported the central bank’s decision to keep interest rates on hold last week, but warned of the possibility that high inflation is a broader problem that could require more aggressive action from policymakers.

item.title: Australia Posts Surprise Trade Surplus as Commodity Exports Gain
item.description: Australia unexpectedly recorded a trade surplus in June as the value of exports — underpinned by commodities — jumped the most in four years while imports dropped.

item.title: Chinese Renewable Energy Giant Envision Launches Data Center
item.description: Envision Group has commissioned the initial phase of a gigawatt-scale data center in China’s Inner Mongolia, an unusual foray by a renewable energy company into the booming artificial intelligence industry.
